page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.12xlarge is a general-purpose, 9th-generation instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz with one thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 192 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 2850 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and delivers a 25 Gbps baseline network throughput without dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results highlight strong compute and memory subsystem performance. The Neoverse-V3 cores achieve top-decile metrics in Geekbench single-core (2,396.0) and multi-core (28,199.0) tests, as well as software compilation via Clang and compression routines such as single-threaded gzip and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The memory subsystem recorded top-tier scores in Passmark memory and cached small-block reads, alongside strong stress-ng multi-core throughput of 96,246.73. Local I/O and networking capacity translate into 104.04 GB/sec static web serving throughput and 136.39 million Redis SET operations per second.

The 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation avoids hyper-threading contention, producing predictable execution times across compute-intensive threads. While LLM text generation throughput remains modest on small to medium models due to the absence of dedicated tensor accelerators, prompt processing reaches 4,218.03 tokens per second for small models. The inclusion of 2850 GB NVMe local storage provides substantial I/O advantages without requiring external block devices.

This server type is engineered for I/O-intensive database engines, distributed caching nodes, software build farms, high-throughput static web serving, and generalized backend business services that require consistent ARM64 performance with fast local NVMe capacity.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 48 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 physical cores at 3.3 GHz and 192 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the server includes 2850 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage and 25 Gbps baseline networking, operating without discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks show exceptional integer, compilation, and decompression capabilities, backed by top-tier Redis SET operations (136.39 million ops/sec) and database throughput. Its single-thread-per-core topology eliminates hyperthreading overhead, ensuring consistent processing density for demanding multi-core loads. The platform delivers strong qualitative cost efficiency for organizations standardizing on high-density ARM64 deployments requiring fast local scratch storage. AWS m9gd.12xlarge is optimal for relational and in-memory databases, Clang compilation pipelines, high-volume web traffic serving, and containerized microservice architectures.
